THE FIX: A BROKEN RELATIVE .md LINK CRASHES `docume publish` WITH A STACK TRACE instead of being reported as a page the converter refuses. Evidence, reproduced this iteration: a fixture whose README.md linked [Setup Guide](guides/setup.md) with no such file made `publish --dry-run` print "Unhandled exception: System.InvalidOperationException: Relative markdown link 'guides/setup.md' does not resolve to any known wiki page (broken cross-reference)" plus 20 stack frames. ROOT CAUSE, both halves confirmed by reading: src/DocuMe.Core/Markdown/ConfluenceStorageRenderer.cs:1567 throws InvalidOperationException for an unresolvable link, and src/DocuMe.Core/Publishing/PublishPipeline.cs:208 catches ONLY NotSupportedException ("the converter's fail-loud contract (§7) is the only exception it throws by design"). So this one construct bypasses the PageConversionFailure path that every other refusal uses. THE RIGHT FIX IS THE THROW, NOT THE CATCH: a broken cross-reference is authored content the converter refuses, which is exactly what NotSupportedException means here, and changing it makes the page land in report.Failures and print under "PAGES THE CONVERTER REFUSES" with the other refusals. The sibling throw two lines above (LinkResolver is null) is genuinely an InvalidOperationException — that one is a programming error, not authored content, so LEAVE IT. Check the same file for other InvalidOperationException throws reachable from authored markdown before deciding the fix is one line; grep found only these two around 1560-1569 but the file is 2000+ lines. Add a test in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Publishing/PublishPipelineTests.cs asserting the broken link becomes a PageConversionFailure naming the link, not an exception — a converter test alone would not catch the regression, because the bug is which exception type crosses the pipeline boundary.

IMPLEMENTATION (two small changes in ConfluenceStorageRenderer.cs): HtmlEntityInlineRenderer, registered after LiteralInlineRenderer and well before the catch-all, writes Markdig's Transcoded value through the existing WriteEscaped; FlattenAltText gains 'case HtmlEntityInline' appending Transcoded, so an entity in image ALT TEXT stops throwing "no plain-text projection". DECISION FOR .claude/references/decisions.md (PENDING — the headless loop cannot write .claude/): ## 2026-07-24 — HTML entities: publish the resolved character, not the entity name A named or numeric character reference is published as the character it resolves to (Markdig's HtmlEntityInline.Transcoded), written back through WriteEscaped, rather than echoed as the source spelling. WHY: storage format is XML, and XML predefines only five entity names (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos). An HTML-only name such as © or   is UNDEFINED in an XML document, so echoing it invites Confluence to reject the body or silently rewrite it on save. A server-side rewrite is §8 content-hash drift, which invalidates an approval when nothing really changed (§9.2). Resolved characters are plain UTF-8 and unambiguous. This is the same reasoning as the strikethrough decision, which emits the editor's own rather than the shape that reads best in source. CONSEQUENCE: re-escaping keeps the round-trip honest. & transcodes to '&' and is written back as '&', never '&'. &/</> come out byte-identical; "/' resolve to a bare " and ', which need no escaping in element content and are re-escaped by WriteAttributeEscaped when the text lands in an attribute instead. CONSEQUENCE TO WATCH IN THE SANDBOX: page bodies now contain non-ASCII characters (©, —, →, …, U+00A0, astral codepoints). Confirm Confluence round-trips them byte-identically on save rather than re-encoding them as numeric character references. U+00A0 is the likeliest to be normalized by the editor. A re-encode would be §8 hash drift on any page containing a symbol. NOT DECIDED HERE: an unrecognized reference. Markdig never makes a node for '&nosuchthing;' or '©' with no semicolon — it leaves a LiteralInline, which already published correctly escaped, so no code was needed and none was written. PROBE FINDINGS (25 cases, tree + output per case; the method's 6th consecutive win, and used TWICE this slice — once before the fix to find the shape, once after to confirm all 25 rendered correctly before a single golden byte was written, which is why the golden matched first try): - Transcodings confirmed rather than assumed: ©/©/© -> U+00A9; ® U+00AE; ™ U+2122; — U+2014; → U+2192; … U+2026;   U+00A0; ' U+0027; " U+0022; 😀 -> SURROGATE PAIR U+D83D U+DE00, which WriteEscaped passes through intact because it writes chars consecutively to one writer. - ALREADY WORKING, NEEDED NOTHING: an entity in a LINK TITLE or a LINK URL (Markdig transcodes those into the string properties before the renderer sees them); an entity in a code span (never entity-parsed, so `©` -> ©); an entity in a FENCE (CDATA, survives verbatim); an unrecognized reference (stays LiteralInline). - THE ONE EXTRA BREAKAGE THE HANDOFF PREDICTED AND THE PROBE CONFIRMED: image alt text threw from FlattenAltText's default case, a different exception from a different call site, so '![a © b](p.png)' would still have failed if only the renderer had been added. DECISIONS PINNED BY TESTS: (1) Resolved character over source spelling (above). (2)   IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE GOLDEN, and this is the slice's second real call. U+00A0 is invisible in a golden file, so a hand review (§4.3) could not tell it from a plain space, and a golden nobody can review by hand fails the rule's whole purpose. Pinned instead by Convert_resolves_nbsp_to_a_non_breaking_space, which spells the escape out explicitly in the C# literal. A dropped HTML comment inside entities.md (free since slice 12) records the omission and names the test, so the gap reads as deliberate rather than forgotten. DO NOT "complete" the golden by adding an   line. (3) THREE MORE FACTS A GOLDEN CANNOT EXPRESS: no double-escaping of &; '<script>' cannot smuggle live markup into the body (matters for §0.2, since Confluence content echoed back into a page is untrusted input); and '"' in image alt text is re-escaped by WriteAttributeEscaped so it cannot break out of the ac:alt attribute.
